description: Three lessons that would have changed the history of my second business if I had learned them earlier.
transcript: Three lessons I learned from my second failed business and number three is actually what killed it. This is the first video of the series of how to make a billion. I started a street clothing company with my friend and we were not making clothes on ourselves. We found a clothes, we found someone who can make it, we found someone who can print on it and we found someone who can distribute it. Lesson number one, you don't trust your suppliers. Consultants are great but they don't have any responsibility for their advices and sometimes they will give give you a bad advice. That's what happened to us, and you are the one being only responsible for that. Lesson number two, you should own your distribution. It's easy to go to the shop and agree with them to sell your stuff. But one day they may decide to raise the prices. One day they decide to put your clothes out of the shelf, and you have no control. If your business depends on it, you'll be in a bit of trouble. And lesson number three three you should have a space for a second mistake you don't go all in i know that you need of economics requires us to go in larger scale so it will be more profitable but if you have no chance to recover that will be a collapse of your business and that's what happened to us next time i'll tell you the lessons i learned from my third failed business and stay tuned
